gen-gf-love-ya-like-a-sister-gf-noto-san: Noto Sans Psalter Pahlavi has gaping e shapes and low-slung capitals that keep it friendly. Love Ya Like A Sister pushes in with chunky, uniform-width strokes, and the sans underneath is lighter, so the two trade places easily.
Bent tubing meets glass portholes. Love Ya Like A Sister draws every letter in one gauge, and Noto Sans Rejang opens its lowercase wide, though a small heading would lose that bold tubing look fast.

Noto Sans Runic carries a big x-height and curves that never close back on themselves. Yet Love Ya Like A Sister holds a drafting-pen line throughout, and that steady, expressive heading is the thing you remember.

Approachable is the first word for Noto Sans Samaritan, whose curves leave plenty of daylight inside. But Love Ya Like A Sister brings the loud, thick-only outline, and that heavy-against-light gap is the pair's strongest quality.

Clean lines run through Noto Sans Saurashtra, with capitals that barely top their neighbors. And Love Ya Like A Sister, with its rounded cord-like strokes, loves a large heading, so give the body the extra size when you want it to hold its own.

Strips of equal width, cut like paper, make up Love Ya Like A Sister and give it bold character. But Noto Sans SC is the surprise: chalky curves that stop short of closing, which makes the pair's strongest quality its loose, easy look.
Bold and blunt, every stroke a single width. Love Ya Like A Sister sets the tone, and Noto Sans Sharada follows with open c forms and bulky lowercase that read like a plain sans.

Noto Sans Siddham brings a generous central band to the text line. Its hanging s ends sit well against Love Ya Like A Sister, a rope-thin outline with no thick or thin parts, and that contrast of lively and plain sans is the strongest thing here.
Noto Sans Sinhala lays a thick, dark stripe of lowercase through every line, with curve endings that stay well apart from each other. Love Ya Like A Sister sits above it, bold throughout.
Noto Sans Soyombo has a sizable x-height made for screens, and its curved letters keep wide, unclosed mouths. Love Ya Like A Sister earns its place big and short, never varying in weight.
